geography.text: Russia's Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth, holding about a fifth of all lake and river water.
The Nile flows north through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea.
The Amazon carries more water than any other river on Earth.
Mount Everest sits on the border of Nepal and China and is the highest peak above sea level.
The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land on Earth, over 400 m below sea level.
Vatican City, inside Rome, is the smallest country in the world by area.
Russia is the largest country in the world and spans 11 time zones.
Australia's capital is Canberra, built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.
Istanbul is split by the Bosphorus, so the city lies in both Europe and Asia.
The Danube flows through more countries than any other river, about ten in all.
Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.
Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.
Venezuela's Angel Falls is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth, about the size of the United States.
Antarctica is the coldest, windiest and driest continent. Much of it is technically a desert.
Chile's Atacama is one of the driest places on Earth. Some weather stations have never recorded rain.
La Paz, Bolivia, at about 3,600 m, is the highest seat of government in the world.
Greenland is the world's largest island that is not a continent.
Indonesia is made of more than 17,000 islands.
Lake Titicaca, on the Peru-Bolivia border, is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.
Ships in the Panama Canal are lifted about 26 m by locks to cross Gatun Lake.
The Suez Canal opened in 1869, linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas.
The Great Wall of China is not one wall but many walls built over about 2,000 years.
Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 1400s high in the Andes of Peru.
Petra in Jordan is a city carved into rose-colored sandstone cliffs.
Cambodia's Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world and appears on its flag.
Reykjavik, Iceland, is the northernmost capital of a sovereign country.
Wellington, New Zealand, is the southernmost capital of a sovereign country.
The Pacific is the largest ocean, bigger than all the land on Earth combined.
The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest part of the ocean, nearly 11 km down.
The equator crosses about a dozen countries, including Ecuador, which is named for it.
Mont Blanc, on the France-Italy border, is the highest mountain in the Alps.
Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is Africa's highest peak and the tallest free-standing mountain.
The Andes are the longest continental mountain range in the world.
Venice is built on more than 100 small islands linked by about 400 bridges.
About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, protected by dikes.
Norway's coast is lined with fjords, deep sea inlets carved by Ice Age glaciers.
Together, the Mississippi and Missouri form one of the longest river systems in the world.
Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.
The Colorado River carved Arizona's Grand Canyon, which is over 1.6 km deep in places.
Four Corners is the only spot where four US states meet: Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah.
Alaska's Denali is the highest mountain in North America.
Hawaii is the only US state made entirely of islands.
Australia is the only country that is also a whole continent.
The Great Barrier Reef off Australia is the largest coral reef system in the world.
Most of Madagascar's wildlife, like its lemurs, is found nowhere else on Earth.
Victoria Falls lies on the Zambezi River between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
The Nile and Amazon are the longest rivers. Which wins depends on how you measure.
Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world and the most densely populated.
San Marino, inside Italy, claims to be the oldest republic in the world.
Cabo da Roca in Portugal is the westernmost point of mainland Europe.
Only about 14 km of water separate Spain and Morocco at the Strait of Gibraltar.
The Caspian Sea is the largest inland body of water on Earth.
Chile is over 4,000 km long but nowhere more than about 350 km wide.
Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
Japan is made of four main islands and thousands of smaller ones.
Mongolia is the most sparsely populated country in the world.
The Ural Mountains are the traditional boundary between Europe and Asia.
The Prime Meridian, 0 degrees longitude, runs through Greenwich in London.
Mount Fuji is Japan's highest peak and an active volcano that last erupted in 1707.
Uluru is a huge sandstone rock in Australia's outback, sacred to the Anangu people.
Ecuador's Galapagos Islands inspired Charles Darwin's ideas on evolution.

geology.text: Igneous rock forms from magma, sedimentary from layers, metamorphic from heat.
Granite cooled slowly deep underground, which gave it its large, visible crystals.
Basalt is the most common rock on the ocean floor. It forms from fast-cooling lava.
Obsidian is volcanic glass. Lava cooled so fast that crystals had no time to grow.
Pumice is so full of gas bubbles that it can float on water.
Marble is limestone changed by heat and pressure. Michelangelo's David is Carrara marble.
Diamond is the hardest natural mineral, a 10 on the Mohs scale. It is pure carbon.
Graphite in pencils is also pure carbon, just like diamond, with its atoms arranged differently.
The Mohs scale ranks minerals from talc, the softest at 1, to diamond, the hardest at 10.
Quartz is one of the most common minerals in Earth's crust and is used in watches.
Feldspars are the most abundant group of minerals in Earth's crust.
Oxygen is the most common element in Earth's crust, followed by silicon.
Earth's core is mostly iron and nickel. The inner core is solid; the outer core is liquid.
Swirling liquid iron in the outer core creates Earth's magnetic field.
About 250 million years ago all the continents were joined as one: Pangaea.
Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, noting how South America and Africa fit together.
Earth's plates move a few centimeters a year, about as fast as your fingernails grow.
The Pacific Ring of Fire is home to most of the world's active volcanoes and largest earthquakes.
The Himalayas formed when India collided with Asia, and they are still rising.
The summit of Everest is made of limestone holding fossils of ancient sea creatures.
The Atlantic widens a few centimeters a year as plates spread apart along this ridge.
Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. At Thingvellir you can walk between two plates.
Here the Pacific and North American plates grind past each other in California.
Measured from its base on the sea floor, Hawaii's Mauna Kea is taller than Everest.
Hawaii's Mauna Loa is the largest active volcano on Earth by volume.
Shield volcanoes, like those in Hawaii, have gentle slopes built from runny lava flows.
Mount Vesuvius buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash in the year 79 AD.
The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa was heard nearly 5,000 km away.
Mount St. Helens erupted in 1980, and its north side collapsed in a huge landslide.
Yellowstone sits on a supervolcano and has about half the world's geysers.
Old Faithful geyser in Yellowstone erupts about every hour and a half.
The word geyser comes from Geysir, a hot spring in Iceland.
Sicily's Mount Etna is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.
Surtsey, off Iceland, is a new island born from an undersea eruption in 1963.
In 1943 the Paricutin volcano grew out of a Mexican cornfield, witnessed from its birth.
Northern Ireland's Giant's Causeway is made of about 40,000 basalt columns from ancient lava.
Stalactites hang from cave ceilings; stalagmites rise from the floor.
Most caves form when slightly acidic water slowly dissolves limestone.
Kentucky's Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave system in the world.
Glaciers carve U-shaped valleys, while rivers cut V-shaped ones.
The Great Lakes were scooped out by Ice Age glaciers.
The oldest rocks at the bottom of the Grand Canyon are nearly 2 billion years old.
Earth is about 4.5 billion years old.
Zircons from Australia's Jack Hills are 4.4 billion years old: Earth's oldest crystals.
Fossils are found mainly in sedimentary rocks like limestone, shale and sandstone.
Amber is fossilized tree resin and sometimes holds insects millions of years old.
In petrified wood, minerals replaced the wood so precisely that tree rings still show.
Coal formed from swamp plants buried hundreds of millions of years ago.
Gold is so soft and malleable that one gram can be beaten into a sheet about a square meter.
Rubies and sapphires are the same mineral, corundum. Only their trace elements differ.
Emerald is a green variety of the mineral beryl, colored by chromium or vanadium.
Amethyst is purple quartz, colored by traces of iron and natural radiation.
Geodes look like plain rocks outside but are hollow and lined with crystals inside.
Table salt is the mineral halite. Its crystals form perfect little cubes.
Mica splits into thin, clear sheets and was once used for windows in stoves.
Each step up on the magnitude scale means about 32 times more energy released.
The strongest earthquake ever recorded struck Chile in 1960, at magnitude 9.5.
Tsunamis are usually caused by undersea earthquakes and can cross whole oceans.
Arizona's Meteor Crater was blasted out by a meteorite about 50,000 years ago.
Utah's Bryce Canyon is famous for hoodoos, tall rock spires shaped by frost and rain.
Most beach sand is tiny grains of quartz worn down from rocks over time.
Hawaii has black sand beaches made from basalt lava that shattered on hitting the sea.
